identity.description: The original (1987 Schmittlein-Morrison-Colombo) buy-till-you-die model and BG/NBD's continuous-time sibling: Poisson purchasing while alive with Gamma heterogeneity, and exponentially distributed customer lifetimes with Gamma heterogeneity (Pareto-II dropout). Dropout can occur at any instant — so P(alive) is an exact continuous-time posterior, well-defined and informative even for zero-repeat customers.

axes.taskNote: UNCERTAINTY (U2/U3): same as bg_nbd — no `clv` task value exists; `regression` (expected future purchase count) chosen with `survival` secondary (the exponential-lifetime dropout submodel IS a survival mechanism, more literally here than in bg_nbd). Dedicated `clv`/`latent-attrition` task value proposed for the U2 agenda.

consumes.note: same contract as bg_nbd: consumed VIA the Doc-2-placed event-log→RFM summary transformation (lifetimes.utils.summary_data_from_transaction_data); the fitter's true input is the (frequency, recency, T) triple. portTypeProposal (U2): `rfm-summary`. targetSpec `none` — the likelihood is over the event history itself

emits.note: conditional_probability_alive — the EXACT continuous-time posterior; unlike bg_nbd it is < 1 for zero-repeat customers, because dropout can occur at any instant rather than only after a purchase
conditional_expected_number_of_purchases_up_to_time(t) — expected transactions over a future horizon t (predict-time argument); lifetimes surfaces the expectation only

the fitted (r, α, s, β) ARE meaningful outputs (family truth: paramsAsOutput): r/α = cohort mean purchase rate, s/β = cohort mean dropout rate — the purchase and death processes read directly off the params. lifetimes exposes params_ (SEs where the summary is available)

the fitted transaction model is a consumable — interchangeable with bg_nbd as gamma_gamma's customer_lifetime_value transaction model. UNCERTAINTY (U2): implicit-vs-declared trained-model emission, same as bg_nbd

penalizer_coef.note: L2 penalty on the four params; more often needed than in bg_nbd because the Pareto/NBD likelihood is a materially harder optimization

invariances.why: inverse sense, as in bg_nbd: frequency/recency/T are literal counts and durations inside the likelihood — standardization corrupts them; consistent time-unit changes are absorbed by the rate parameters (α, β). FLAGGED for U3: the boolean cannot express 'requires raw units'
nonlinear transforms of recency/T change the exponential inter-purchase and lifetime structure the likelihood assumes
the likelihood needs a complete (frequency, recency, T) triple; NaN in an RFM summary signals an upstream featurizer defect — reject, don't impute
covariate-free — heterogeneity enters only through the two Gamma mixing distributions
four explicit commitments: Poisson purchasing while alive, Gamma-distributed purchase rates, exponentially distributed lifetimes, Gamma-distributed death rates
identification comes from cohort breadth, not per-customer depth; hierarchical shrinkage handles sparse individual histories — and zero-repeat customers still contribute dropout information here
the fitted point process projects expected transactions and aliveness over any future horizon — the model exists to extrapolate beyond the observation window

featureStats.why: the dropout pair (s, β) is identified from the joint frequency-recency pattern; low repeat rates weaken it, though — unlike bg_nbd — a silent zero-repeat customer is still evidence about death, since dropout can occur at any instant
variance/mean of repeat counts; the shared Gamma-Poisson purchase submodel exists to absorb overdispersion — a ratio near 1 says heterogeneity is weak
the recency-based alive/dead separation needs T long relative to typical inter-purchase gaps; short windows leave the continuous-time posterior prior-driven

modelMetrics.why: expected vs actual holdout transactions per customer — the canonical BTYD validation for a model whose churn is latent
predicted vs observed repeat-frequency histogram on the calibration window; misfit here indicts the Poisson-Gamma purchase commitment directly

edgeCases.behavior: the likelihood's Gauss hypergeometric term (2F1) overflows / loses precision at extremes despite lifetimes' log-space evaluation
edgeCases.note: rescale time to coarser units (days→weeks) and/or add penalizer_coef

edgeCases.behavior: degenerate or impossible RFM summary — invalid likelihood contribution
(s, β) weakly identified — wide CIs, unstable P(alive); NOT flat as in bg_nbd, since zero-repeat customers still carry dropout information
the Pareto/NBD MLE is documented as substantially harder than BG/NBD's; fits can stall or diverge without penalization
edgeCases.note: penalizer_coef; bg_nbd as the fallback transaction model

driver.depNote: UNCERTAINTY (dep choice): lifetimes is in maintenance mode; pymc-marketing's clv.ParetoNBDModel is the maintained successor (heavier PyMC dep; MCMC fit non-deterministic). Sheet written against lifetimes; flagged for family-level review
driver.wrapperNeeds: the event-log→RFM featurizer is a SEPARATE upstream component; predict maps to conditional_probability_alive / conditional_expected_number_of_purchases_up_to_time(t); numerical guard for the 2F1 term (time-unit rescaling) belongs in the wrapper
driver.threadSafety: single-threaded fit; predictions are pure functions of the four fitted params — safe to parallelize after fit

canBeSeeds.note: interchangeable with bg_nbd as the transaction half of gamma_gamma's CLV composition

placementClaims.why: the RFM featurizer emits complete summaries by construction; a missing transaction is unobservable, not imputable
nonlinear transforms of frequency/recency/T corrupt the count/duration semantics the likelihood is written in
standardization destroys the raw units the Poisson/exponential machinery requires; only consistent time-unit changes are legal (absorbed by α, β)
no categorical covariates exist in the input contract — the model is covariate-free
